instructions: Put the 1/2 cup rice in a bowl, cover it with cold water and leave it to soak for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, chop 1/4 cup of the mint leaves and 1/4 cup of the parsley leaves. Mince the 4 garlic cloves and keep them in two piles of 2.
Dice the onion. Seed and chop the poblano. Peel and dice the 2 carrots, cut the 2 potatoes into 1 inch pieces and dice the zucchini.

Drain the rice in a sieve and rinse it. Put it in a large bowl with the 1 lb beef, the egg, the mint, the parsley, one pile of the garlic, the 1 1/4 tsp cumin, the 1 1/4 tsp onion powder, the 1/2 tsp oregano, 3/4 tsp of the salt and the 1/2 tsp pepper.

Mix it with your hands until it's evenly combined, then stop. Any longer and the meatballs come out tough. Roll it into balls about 1 1/2 inches across, which makes about 20, and put them on a plate in the fridge.
Heat the 2 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft. Add the poblano and cook for 1 minute.
Add the second pile of garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until you can smell it. Stir in the carrots and the can of tomatoes with their juice and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the 4 cups broth and 2 cups water. Add the potatoes and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and bring it to a boil over high.
Lower the meatballs into the soup one at a time with a spoon. Turn the heat down so it simmers gently, cover the pot and cook for 15 minutes. Don't stir. The meatballs are soft until they set.

Add the zucchini, cover again and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the rice in the meatballs is soft. You're cooking the meatballs to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut one in half: it's done when there's no pink left.
Warm each tortilla in a dry skillet over medium for about 30 seconds, flip it and warm the other side for 30 seconds. Stack them in a clean towel as you go.
Turn off the heat. Chop a small handful of the parsley and scatter it over the soup. Taste the broth. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle the soup into bowls with a few meatballs in each and serve with the warm tortillas.
method_notes: All three read versions mix raw rice into the beef meatballs with an egg, fresh herbs and cumin, then simmer them in a tomato and chicken broth soup with carrots, potatoes and zucchini without stirring until they set. Posh Journal soaks the rice first, seasons the meatballs with spearmint, parsley, cumin, onion powder and oregano, and builds the soup on onion, serrano, garlic and canned tomatoes, adding the zucchini halfway. Slender Kitchen adds celery, tomato paste and corn, and Sandra Valvassori mixes beef with ground chicken and adds cilantro. This one follows Posh Journal and uses its own swap of a poblano for the serranos so the pot stays mild.
